document_check.note: Harvey PD et al., Psychiatry Research 334 (2024) 115792, 'Improvements in performance based measures of functional capacity and cognition after computerized functional skills training in older people with mild cognitive impairment and healthy comparators'. It is a randomised trial in which MCI participants were randomised to FUNSAT functional skills training alone or FUNSAT preceded by a 3-week CCT burst. The cited figure (no difference between the MCI arms on composite cognition, p = 0.39) is on p.5.

cited_result: Within the MCI group, the randomised comparison of combined training (3-week Brain HQ CCT burst followed by FUNSAT) against FUNSAT skills training alone on change in BAC-app composite cognition: 'no training condition differences within the MCI group for composite cognition, t = 0.86, p = 0.39' (p.5).
tool_reason: The cited result is a randomised between-arm comparison (combined vs single-modality training) within the MCI stratum of a trial, so RoB 2 applies for the composite-cognition outcome.

domains.rationale: The trial is described as randomised, but neither sequence generation nor allocation concealment is reported. Among completers, baseline composite cognition and VRFCAT are similar across arms, and demographics are not reported by arm.

signalling.question: 1.1 Was the allocation sequence random?
signalling.quote: MCI participants were randomized to either receive FUNSAT training only or to receive a three-week burst of CCT prior to the initiation of FUNSAT.

signalling.question: 1.2 Was the allocation sequence concealed until participants were enrolled and assigned?
signalling.quote: Searched for concealment, envelopes, central allocation, randomisation method: none reported. Only: 'The MCI participants were randomized to receive FUNSAT™ training alone or in combination with a burst of CCT.'

signalling.question: 1.3 Did baseline differences between intervention groups suggest a problem with randomisation?
signalling.quote: MCI Skills only −1.07 0.63 ... MCI Combined −1.15 0.61 (baseline composite cognition, Table 2, 'analysis of cases who competed all three assessments'); VRFCAT baseline 1316.99 vs 1333.08

domains.domain: D2 Deviations from intended interventions (effect of assignment)
domains.rationale: The design was open: participants trained at home and the staff were company employees, with no blinding reported. The analysis is of completers only, not of everyone as randomised. About 9% of the MCI participants (84 of 92 analysed) were excluded, and the split between arms is not reported.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were participants aware of their assigned intervention during the trial?
signalling.quote: Participants independently completed up to 12 weeks of computerized training at home after screening, informed consent, and an in-person baseline evaluation

signalling.question: 2.2 Were carers and people delivering the interventions aware of participants' assigned intervention?
signalling.quote: Ms. Chirino, Mr. Zayas-Bayan, and Ms. Mueller, as well as Dr. Rivera-Molina were full time employees of i-Function during the time that this data was collected. (No blinding of staff reported.)

signalling.question: 2.3 Were there deviations from the intended intervention that arose because of the trial context?
signalling.quote: Completion rate for training was 92 % for MCI participants who initiated training and 96 % for the NC. (Deviations by arm not reported.)

signalling.question: 2.6 Was an appropriate analysis used to estimate the effect of assignment to intervention?
signalling.quote: Performance on composite cognitive performance ... separated by training condition: analysis of cases who competed all three assessments. ... MCI (n = 84)

signalling.question: 2.7 Was there potential for a substantial impact (on the result) of the failure to analyse participants in the group to which they were randomised?
signalling.quote: Participants with MCI (N = 92) (Table 1) versus MCI (n = 84) in Table 3: about 9% excluded

domains.rationale: Outcome data are available for about 91% of the MCI participants, with no sensitivity analysis or imputation. Missingness could relate to cognitive status: the authors' own earlier trial had more dropout with combined training in MCI. The reported losses are small, however.

signalling.question: 3.1 Were data for this outcome available for all, or nearly all, participants randomised?
signalling.quote: MCI (n = 84) (Table 3) of 'Participants with MCI (N = 92)' (Table 1)

signalling.question: 3.2 Is there evidence that the result was not biased by missing outcome data?
signalling.quote: We also compared training gains from baseline to endpoint between MCI participants across the two training conditions on composite cognition and VRFCAT time to completion using t-tests. (Searched for imputation or sensitivity analysis: none.)

signalling.question: 3.3 Could missingness in the outcome depend on its true value?
signalling.quote: participants with MCI showed a greater dropout rate than NC, particularly with combined training (Harvey et al., 2022)

signalling.question: 3.4 Is it likely that missingness in the outcome depended on its true value?
signalling.quote: There were two MCI participants and 1 NC who did not complete the follow-up assessment.

domains.rationale: The outcome is a validated performance battery given identically to both arms. Blinding of the outcome assessors is not reported, and the battery includes tester-administered verbal tasks. The timing of the post-training assessment depended on mastery, which differed by arm.

signalling.question: 4.1 Was the method of measuring the outcome inappropriate?
signalling.quote: The original paper version of the BAC assesses cognitive areas that are linked to daily functioning (Keefe et al., 2004). For simplicity of administration and uniformity, the same evaluations are delivered via a tablet linked to the cloud with the BAC App

signalling.question: 4.2 Could measurement or ascertainment of the outcome have differed between intervention groups?
signalling.quote: Participants were reassessed remotely with Form B of the fixed-difficulty assessments at the conclusion of the 12-week training period or following mastery of all six training tasks.

signalling.question: 4.3 Were outcome assessors aware of the intervention received by study participants?
signalling.quote: Searched for blind/masked assessors: none. Only 'testing performed by bilingual testers and training and assessments performed in the same language.'

signalling.question: 4.4 Could assessment of the outcome have been influenced by knowledge of intervention received?
signalling.quote: Verbal Fluency: Measures category fluency (animals) and letter fluency (F and S). Dependent variable was the total score for 3 60-second blocks

signalling.question: 4.5 Is it likely that assessment of the outcome was influenced by knowledge of intervention received?
signalling.quote: We used three different alternative forms of the BAC app; previous studies have shown retest effects across forms that were less than 0.1 SD for composite scores.

domains.domain: D5 Selection of the reported result
domains.rationale: The trial is registered and its outcomes are called pre-planned, but no statistical analysis plan is cited. The composite was constructed for this paper, and the 'endpoint' time point used for the arm comparison (post-training or 30-day) is not specified. Elsewhere in the paper, analysis choices were data-driven.

signalling.question: 5.1 Were the data analysed in accordance with a pre-specified analysis plan finalised before unblinded outcome data were available?
signalling.quote: This trial (NCT046779441) had three different pre-planned outcomes, presented separately.

signalling.question: 5.2 Was the result likely selected from multiple eligible outcome measurements?
signalling.quote: Because we had a sample of participants that was older and composed of a heterogenous group of minority and non-minority participants, we created a composite score for the performance of the NC sample.

signalling.question: 5.3 Was the result likely selected from multiple eligible analyses of the data?
signalling.quote: Following up this interaction, we repeated the analysis, eliminating total training as a covariate.

overall: High risk of bias (some concerns in all five domains)
overall_rationale: All five domains carry some concerns: randomisation and concealment are unreported, the design was open, the analysis is of completers only, outcome assessors were not blinded, and there is no pre-specified analysis plan for this comparison. Under RoB 2 and this review's rule, some concerns in several domains gives an overall high risk of bias. There is also an undeclared-in-design but disclosed commercial interest: every author is an officer or employee of the company that licenses FUNSAT.

applicability.concern: The 'single-modality' arm is FUNSAT functional skills training, not cognitive training
applicability.rationale: The combined arm adds a 3-week Brain HQ processing-speed burst before FUNSAT. It is a head-to-head test of adding CCT to skills training, not of intensified versus single CCT.

applicability.concern: MCI defined by Jak-Bondi criteria in a bilingual community sample, MoCA 18 or above
applicability.rationale: The subtype mix (43% non-amnestic) and the exclusion of MoCA < 18 limit generalisation to clinic amnestic MCI.
